Grade: PP2
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: HEALTH

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CARE PRACTICES
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Care PRACTICES helps you succeed in ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: CARE PRACTICES
Study Care PRACTICES like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Care PRACTICES means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Care PRACTICES means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Care PRACTICES means in simple pupil language.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Care PRACTICES” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Care PRACTICES means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Care PRACTICES from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Care PRACTICES from Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Care PRACTICES from Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Care PRACTICES matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Care PRACTICES from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Care PRACTICES in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Care PRACTICES in clear steps. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Care PRACTICES in clear steps.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Care PRACTICES this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Care PRACTICES in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Care PRACTICES in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Care PRACTICES in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Care PRACTICES in one real-life situation this week.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Care PRACTICES” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Care PRACTICES in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Care PRACTICES is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Care PRACTICES” around your school. (skill: explain what Care PRACTICES means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Say why Care PRACTICES matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Care PRACTICES from Kenya)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Care PRACTICES this week. (skill: practise Care PRACTICES in clear steps)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Care PRACTICES” around your school. (skill: apply Care PRACTICES in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Care PRACTICES to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Care PRACTICES means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Care PRACTICES from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Care PRACTICES in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Care PRACTICES from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Care PRACTICES: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Care PRACTICES?
